question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states that it is the duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and to improve public health?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 47**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 47** falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It mandates the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people.
 
• The Article also emphasizes the duty of the State to improve public health.
 
• It reflects the commitment of the State to ensure the well-being of its citizens through appropriate policy measures.
 
• Article 47 specifically focuses on the prohibition of the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health, except for medicinal purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• DPSP are guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Public Health Initiatives in India**
 
 
• India has launched several public health programs such as the National Health Mission (NHM) to improve the healthcare system.
 
• Ayushman Bharat is another significant initiative aimed at providing health coverage and establishing wellness centers across the country.
 
• The Government also focuses on immunization programs to prevent diseases like polio, measles, and tuberculosis.
 
• Sanitation and hygiene campaigns like Swachh Bharat Abhiyan aim to improve public health by promoting cleanliness.
 
 
 
• **Nutrition Programs in India**
 
 
• Programs like the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) aim to improve the nutritional status of children and mothers.
 
• Mid-Day Meal Scheme provides nutritious meals to school children to enhance their nutritional intake and educational outcomes.
 
• POSHAN Abhiyaan is a flagship program to improve nutritional outcomes for children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• The Public Distribution System (PDS) ensures the availability of essential food grains to the poor at subsidized rates.
